review.verdict: The department set a clear charter in 3 AI calls and 0.6 minutes, then correctly paused for the Requester, but it stopped at cycle 0, so Adaptation, Priority, Coordination, Builder and Audit were never exercised.

identity.note: Charter is concrete: 13 observable done-when items, and the open Vercel URL is a labelled placeholder [4]. But [2] bundles three questions into one ASK_CEO when the role says one bounded decision. [4] also hands work to @Adaptation while stating that Requester approval is needed first.

ceo.note: Chose one option per question, gave a one-line reason and named the accepted risk [3]. Did not touch done-when. Q2 picked the last-shown option, so it was not just taking the first one. Weak point: it said the brief was silent on all three, yet Q3 concerns the brief's explicit 'on Vercel' wording.

builder.note: No turns (0), site_bytes 0. Not scorable. 3 is a placeholder.

went_well: Typo in the brief ('sudokou') was handled without fuss; the charter site name is 'Sudoku' [2].
Charter scope is tight: the rules cap work at the CEO's three decisions and forbid persistence or extra features without a new Identity ruling.
Dropping live publishing was surfaced, not hidden. The charter lists it in dropped_from_brief and the validator paused the run [5][6].
Spend was 0 of 100 and there were 0 redirects and 0 invalid moves, so hand-off rules were not strained (thin evidence, 3 agent turns).
problems: Identity asked three questions in one message, against the 'one decision-ready question' rule [2].

The CEO decided to drop an explicit brief item (live Vercel deploy) [3]. That is the Requester's call, so the pause was always going to follow. Identity could have asked the Requester directly, which is cheaper.
[4] tells Adaptation to propose workflows, then [5] and [6] pause the run. The hand-off was wasted and slightly confusing.
[6] says 'Site v0 is in the preview' but site_bytes is 0, so there is nothing to preview.
[5] has a doubled period and asks an open 'keep or drop' question, not a decision-ready A/B.
learnings: Test the post-pause path next. Add a scripted Requester reply (accept the drop) so the run reaches Adaptation, Priority, Builder and Audit. Without it, no workflow design is tested (cycles 0, proposals 0).
Run the dropped-from-brief check before Identity hands off, or have Identity word the hand-off as 'on hold until the Requester answers'. Evidence: [4] versus [5][6].
Ask Identity to put explicit-brief trade-offs to the Requester, and keep the CEO for value trade-offs. Evidence: Q3 [2][3] led straight to the pause.
Do not read the CEO bias metrics yet. 3 decisions: 2 picked the first-shown option and 2 picked Identity's first option. That is too few to conclude anything.
Fix the preview note and message text: do not announce a site version when site_bytes is 0.

events.detail: charter drops brief items: Publishing the game live on Vercel is not part of the charter. The department makes no outward-facing action and holds no Vercel credentials, so it delivers the single index.html plus deploy steps for the Requester to run. The Requester must agree to this before work starts.
